hotspot_events.title: Nvidia falls a seventh straight day, plunging 14% in one session: closed Nov 20 at $125.53 (-14.01%), down about 24.5% over five days
hotspot_events.heat_reason: A 14% single-day plunge, the largest recent drop; seven straight down days totaling about -24.5% in five days and about -43% in November; the board's refusal to reinstate Jensen Huang, the rumored SEC probe and a wave of analyst target cuts stack up
hotspot_events.summary: Nvidia closed Nov 20 at $125.53 (-14.01%, intraday low $124.50), a seventh consecutive down day, about -24.5% over five days and about -43% for November. The board made clear on Nov 17 that it will not reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, and a headhunter is searching for a permanent CEO. The WSJ-reported SEC civil investigation remains unconfirmed. Analysts cut targets in a wave on Nov 18-19; Oppenheimer downgraded to Perform and removed its price target. The stock rebounded to $130.27 after hours (+3.78%).

hotspot_events.title: Copper down more than 10% on the week while spot stays tight: SHFE main contract closed Nov 20 at CNY 92,400/t, weekly -10.06%
hotspot_events.heat_reason: The SHFE main contract's -10.06% week is one of its worst in a decade and LME 3M touched an eight-month low intraday, yet the spot premium is still as high as CNY 6,580/t with inventories at just 54,800 tons - falling futures alongside tight spot
hotspot_events.summary: The SHFE copper main contract closed Nov 20 at CNY 92,400/t (-3.35%), down CNY 10,340 on the week (-10.06%, one of the worst weeks in a decade). LME 3M closed Nov 20 at $12,526/t (+0.44%) after touching $12,020 intraday (an eight-month low), down more than 13% in November. Domestic 1# copper spot premium, however, remains as high as CNY 6,580/t, and electrolytic copper spot inventories are just 54,800 tons.
numbers: SHFE main contract closed Nov 20 at CNY 92,400/t (-3.35%)

hotspot_events.title: Ga/Ge/Sb suspension expires Nov 27 - six days left, still no extension notice
hotspot_events.heat_reason: The suspension under MOFCOM Announcement No. 72 expires Nov 27; as of the morning of Nov 21 there is still no extension notice, with six days left; on expiry, US-bound export licensing reverts to 'not approved in principle'
hotspot_events.summary: The suspension period under MOFCOM Announcement No. 72 runs to Nov 27, 2026, and no extension notice had appeared as of the morning of Nov 21. Announcement No. 58 of Nov 9 extended only the October package of measures to Jan 10, 2027 and did not cover Announcement No. 72. On expiry, US-bound export licensing reverts to 'not approved in principle'.
numbers: Announcement No. 58 extended to Jan 10, 2027; does not cover Announcement No. 72

industry_updates.title: LG creates dedicated AI data-center cooling unit and a Virginia chiller production subsidiary
industry_updates.detail: On Nov 19 LG announced an organizational reshuffle: a new Applied Business unit under its Eco Solution division dedicated to AI data-center cooling, plus a new production subsidiary in Virginia to expand chiller capacity. Background: its US subsidiary has signed long-term orders totaling 5 GW of data-center chillers, and LG targets KRW 1 trillion in annual chiller sales next year.

industry_updates.title: Johnson Controls expands HVAC manufacturing site in Schertz, Texas
industry_updates.detail: On Nov 19 Johnson Controls announced an expansion of its HVAC manufacturing site in Schertz, Texas - investment of more than $179 million, 552 new full-time jobs, and a 536,000 sq ft plant.

industry_updates.title: Modexus investor day sets FY2029 targets of $5.7-7.7B and a $500M buyback
industry_updates.detail: At its Nov 18 investor day, Modexus (formerly Modine) set FY2029 revenue targets of $5.7-7.7 billion (data-center business $4.5-6.5 billion), and its board approved a $500 million share buyback. On Nov 19 it confirmed its headquarters move to Milwaukee's Harbor District. Activist investor Jana Partners is pressing for higher margins or a sale.

industry_updates.title: Lenovo Q2: revenue $30.24B (+48%), ISG $11.3B (+178%)
industry_updates.detail: Lenovo reported Q2 results on Nov 19: revenue of $30.24 billion (up 48% year on year, a record quarter), infrastructure business ISG at $11.3 billion (up 178%), AI-related revenue of $10.8 billion (up 79%), and an AI server order pipeline expanded to $80 billion (up 48% quarter on quarter).

industry_updates.title: Hitachi joins OpenAI cyber-defense partner program
industry_updates.detail: On Nov 20 Hitachi joined OpenAI's 'Daybreak Defense Network' cyber-defense partner program; on Nov 18 Hitachi Digital released its HARC Compose AI platform. Limited supply-chain relevance.

industry_updates.title: CBAM extended to Norway and Iceland; Ga/Ge/Sb suspension still expires Nov 27
industry_updates.detail: On Nov 18 the European Commission announced CBAM will apply from Jan 1, 2027 to aluminum, steel and other goods imported from Norway and Iceland. The suspension of the Ga/Ge/Sb export ban to the US expires Nov 27, with no extension notice as of the morning of Nov 21. Within the window, USTR, the US Department of Commerce, the White House, and China's MOFCOM / General Administration of Customs issued no new finalized HVAC-related measures.
industry_updates.source: European Commission, Directorate-General for Taxation and Customs Union, Nov 18, 2026

siphon_effects.detail: At TrendForce's Nov 18 Seoul roadshow: Q4 commodity DRAM contract prices up 10-15% quarter on quarter and NAND up 15-20%, with further quarterly increases through 2027. HBM4 pricing for 2027 at $3.00-5.50/Gb (vs over $2.05 in 2026, up more than 100%). HBM's share of the big three's DRAM wafer capacity rises from 23% to nearly 30% in 2027.

TrendForce raised its MLCC supply-demand assessment to 'very tight', with lead times of 40 weeks (Meritz says Samsung Electro-Mechanics is at 52 weeks across the board). Samsung Electro-Mechanics had received about KRW 1 trillion ($777 million) in prepayments under long-term supply contracts with big-tech customers by end-Q3. Q3 MLCC average prices rose 21.4% year on year; Q4 consumer-grade X5R average prices to OEMs/ODMs could rise another 25-30% (TrendForce estimate).
siphon_effects.source: TrendForce via NextPCB, Nov 12, 2026; Aju Press, Nov 19, 2026

siphon_effects.detail: Lenovo Q2 ISG revenue of $11.3 billion (up 178% year on year) with an AI server pipeline of $80 billion (up 48% quarter on quarter). Modexus targets $4.5-6.5 billion of FY2029 data-center revenue (60-80% CAGR) and is expanding capacity to $6-7 billion. LG targets KRW 1 trillion in chiller sales next year.
siphon_effects.source: Lenovo, Nov 19, 2026; PRNewswire, Nov 18, 2026; LG, Nov 19, 2026

siphon_effects.detail: High-performance CCL procurement cycles run 24-32 weeks, with shortages of 106/1080/2116 glass cloth and quota-based supply at several makers. Shengyi's November increases landed (M6 and below laminates +15%, prepreg +25%), with production scheduled out to January 2027. Kingboard's eighth increase round this year took November thin electronic cloth up 13-14% month on month. No restart news yet from Panasonic's fire-hit Hukou plant.

Lead times for general power transformers run 24-48 months, and over 36 months for large units. Shihlin Electric's order backlog exceeds NT$60 billion with visibility to 2029-2030; after raising prices 15-20% in March it says further adjustments are coming.

cross_industry.detail: ST's fourth round, NXP's third round and Renesas's adjustment all take effect Jan 1, 2027; magnitudes and part numbers remain undisclosed officially. MCU lead times stay long: ST MCUs about 54 weeks, some Infineon 32-bit MCU parts up to 97 weeks, NXP S32K/S32G at 36-52 weeks.
cross_industry.source: limchip, Nov 11, 2026; LDeepAI citing a Future Electronics October report, Oct 29, 2026

cross_industry.detail: CPCA's Nov 19 forecast puts November NEV retail sales at 1.15 million units with penetration at 70.6%, above 70% for the first time - but the overall market is shrinking (narrow passenger-car retail down 1.1% month on month). Penetration is rising mainly because fuel vehicles are collapsing (October fuel-vehicle retail down 45% year on year). NEVs keep crowding IGBT, automotive-grade MLCC and copper capacity.

Global PC shipments fell 21% year on year in Q3 to 58.1 million units, with Q4 expected down another 24-27%; notebook weakness extends to Q2 2027. Memory's share of PC cost has risen from about 15% to nearly 40%. Shrinking demand frees no capacity - memory and MLCC are allocated to AI first.
cross_industry.source: Omdia via StockWatch, Oct 9, 2026; DIGITIMES, Nov 19, 2026

cross_industry.detail: N-type dense polysilicon held steady at CNY 38-43/kg; wafer declines steepened and modules fell back to CNY 0.7/W. October polysilicon output fell 11.72% month on month. Destocking price pressure creates no upward cost transmission to HVAC.

CME FedWatch as of Nov 20 prices a December hike at 100% (about 94-98% for 25bp, about 2.7-6% for 50bp). October PCE lands Nov 25 (consensus +3.8% year on year, core +3.2%) - the last inflation reading before the Dec 8-9 FOMC.
